The core innovation—adapting Belief MCTS (BAMCP) to continuous spaces via Double Progressive Widening (DPW) and integrating it into a search-based policy iteration framework (AlphaZero-style distillation)—is conceptually sound and addresses a known limitation of previous methods that struggle with the "curse of dimensionality" in belief spaces.

Nevertheless, the substantive contributions—specifically the successful adaptation of BAMCP to continuous offline domains and the strong empirical validation—outweigh the missing theoretical justifications and reproducibility details. The paper is clearly a solid addition to the literature, offering a working, high-performing algorithm where prior attempts struggled.
